I was so looking forward to having this fun little toy to show people. I charged it for a couple of hours and was ready to see how it works. Well, first off, the on/off button is nowhere to be seen. JOY FOR ALL - Orange Tabby Cat - Interactive Companion Pets - Realistic & Lifelike My 75-year-old sister almost died from acute kidney failure following a major flare of autoimmune vasculitis. When I spoke with the doctors, they said she would not be able to keep her pets (two little dogs, two cats) because it would not be safe. She'll be on immunosuppressants from here on out, and exposure to live pets will be too dangerous.

I didn't realize there was such a thing as a robotic companion animal for adults, but a friend of ours said she was looking into a robotic dog from Japan. (Yeah, one of those really expensive futuristic plastic ones.)

I started researching and watching videos on YouTube, and I thought this Joy For All cat would be perfect for her. Her cats have always climbed up on the desk between her iMac monitor and her keyboard drawer and been a constant presence. Joy For All also has a dog version of this companion pet, but knowing my sister, it will be the cats she misses the most. This kitty can lie on her desk and be responsive to her when she needs it but go to sleep when she's embroiled in work.

I just got word my sister's new kitty has been delivered to her home and is waiting for her on the dining room table. She won't be out of rehab for at least a few weeks, but I'm so glad to know she won't be completely alone when she gets back home. I mean, hey, she refers to her Roomba as "My manservant, Raul" and talks to him, so I know she'll be really tickled with this robotic cat. I just thank goodness that these are available. I was really worried that my sister, who has had cats her whole life, was at risk of sinking into a bad depression after all she has been through. But what a great kitty this is! I want one, too!

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

text_fidelity_a:
Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig UPDATE: Oh, the poor little Bandit! Bandit has been Bingo's security blanket, humping companion, BFF, and "only other dog in the house" until we got a real-live lifewire little dog, Doobie, who is a Jack Chi. Doobie is one high-energy chewing fool. Doobie has gotten up inside of Bandit and pulled his guts out of his butt and also chewed his eyes out, leaving holes. Bingo is not happy and so is trying to tug his dear Bandit away from Doobie, so I knew Bandit was not going to be long for the world. I ordered a new Bandit for Bingo, and he is thrilled, but I'm going to have to put him up until Doobie is over his puppy stage. But this Bandit racoon puppet is a fantastic purchase for a little dog.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Move over Gator. Hit the box, Fox. Bandit has arrived.

Our 10-week-old Chiweenie puppy wants to bite-shake play, and even though he's careful not to be too vicious with DH's hand, he was breaking the skin. I got this puppet as a way to protect us from those sharp little puppy teeth.

Bingo went nuts for Bandit, and we did, too. On my hand, I don't like the fit on my thumb, which tends to slide out of the arm, but it seems to be fine on DH's larger hand. I just lift Bandit by the back and march him up and down, and the puppet is floppy enough, but also firm enough, to seem like a living critter.

I can't emphasize enough how nice the contrast between his nose and white snout is. When we say "bite his nose," he goes right for that little black nose. The nose and the eyes are sewn in very well so I don't worry so much about our dog pulling them off and choking them. Another thing really nice about this puppet is that it has some movement to it even when we are not assisting him in playing with it. He will pick it up and shake it, carry it around like it's his prize possession (which is funny, because it's bigger than he is), and put it in his "room" (a small rug) with his collection of squirrels and such.

UPDATE: Oh, Bandit is such a hit! Bingo sleeps with Bandit, pees on Bandit, madly humps Bandit, chases him all over the house when we throw him, carries him proudly to show "Bingo too" in the mirror, jumps up into the back of the loveseat in the living room with Bandit so Bandit can look out the window with Bingo at the neighbors passing by. Bandit has had to go in the washing machine quite a few times now, and with vicious chiweenie tug-of-war play, poor Bandit's scalp is starting to come unsewn. I can sew him up by hand and he'll be fine, but I'm already thinking I'd better get another Bandit to have on hand for when Bingo's BFF is in complete shreds! Bandit has shrunk some with washing, so it's hard to get a large adult hand into him, but he's still more than doing his job. He and Bingo now are about the same size. Bingo's eight months old and seven pounds.
text_fidelity_b: Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig

So Slime DIY - Mini Slime Caddy Our library has monthly slime making labs that my children enjoy. It's created a greater interest in the world of slime for them and it's something fun for us to enjoy when boredom strikes, especially in the late evening/night hours. This kit was enjoyed by all of us. It comes with a little caddy(and a removeable tray) to hold the supplies. Inside, there are two containers for making the slime, stickers for decorating the containers, 4 packs of slime powder, 4 packs of decoration(glitter and small shapes), and 2 little toys(ours isn't what's shown...star and cloud here). To make the slime, all the maker has to do is add the slime powder and any glitter/shapes they want, then fill to the line with water, put the top on, *hold* it on well, and then shake it until it's the right consistency. We had to shake longer than the directions said, but it still doesn't take long and it's super easy.

Just to note, the glitter still gets everywhere. It doesn't stick to the slime like I thought it would. While playing with the slime, it came off on our hands a great deal. I found glitter everywhere afterwards, despite us trying to be careful with it. It was on us, the table, the floor, the couches. My husband wasn't even here when we made it, nor did he play with it, but he even ended up with glitter on his face the next day. So, keep that in mind if you dislike glitter as much as I do. Too, my children didn't like the shapes in the slime, saying it poked their hands. It comes off the slime, too. Otherwise, we've enjoyed it!
text_fidelity_b: So Slime DIY - Mini Slime Caddy

text_fidelity_a:
HUBSAN X4 H107C HD 2MP Camera 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter Red/White (PH-H107C) At first I received the SD version instead of the HD version from one seller on Amazon. I returned it.The Little One's Choice got it right and sent me the HD version for which I had paid. Make sure you get what you paid for. It should say "HD Camera" in big letters on the Hubsan box. Unfortunately, the correct one they sent had horrible very dark lines in the video in all types of lighting conditions. I had to return it. The replacement was fine.

My "review" is going to be a bit rambling from an experienced guy to those who are tying to get started in this hobby. My hope is that I might have something to say that the old-timers might find useful as well.

My short review in this paragraph is that this quad is awesome (overused word, I know, but it fits here) for the price and simply amazing. I've had hours of fun with mine and I own 2 other non-camera Hubsans, one Proto-X and a Blade Quad Nano. This Hubsan quad is the most bang for the buck. I've also got big copters that are gathering dust while I have fun with these small ones. Strangely, I'm not missing them. Did I mention these little things are fun?

It is refreshing to the point of joyfulness to be able to fly this quad around since it is so relatively inexpensive and nimble. I bought several bags of props out of an abundance of caution and have not used one yet. Still, I don't crash much, so if you are new at this, you might need more propellers than the one set provided. I bought some spare batteries (they are blue, sold in a set of 5) and a couple of the Traxxas 2-port chargers. These work fine and let you have more charged batteries handy.

I want to say this quad is easy to fly. For me it is very easy, but it is also fun. I understand that for those who have never flown any type of RC rotor craft that you will have to be serious about learning to use and fly this little thing properly.

Don't be frustrated if you crash a lot at first. Fly in an open area outdoors if possible. If you fly indoors, which I know is a very attractive prospect at first, you will crash into walls and ceiling often and perhaps lose some propellers. At first you may even forget which hand "does what" and crash pretty hard. The body of this quad is tough, but I have seen some photos of broken ones. All of those slammed hard onto concrete walls or slabs.

If a crash is imminent, learn to cut the power immediately. Throttle off completely. You do not want the motors stalling against an obstruction. They will burn out if you abuse them that way. Also, never try to bump the throttle to kick the motors on in an attempt to flip the copter upright if it sets down at an angle. Motivate your body to the quad, pick it up and set it down straight. It will last longer that way.

The rotor guard is taped to the bottom of the tray. Use it if you are unsure of your skills. By the way, when removing the props to put this on, do be sure to hold down the motor body. If it comes up too far the motor wires will snap off. It is only held in place with friction. Use a pinching grasp to pull the prop off. There's a little wrench to help with pulling the props. Use that if one came with your quad. Some people don't get one, I don't know why.

This same type of grasp is also the correct way to disconnect the battery. If you pull by the wires, you will soon have a broken connection. Try to grasp both sides of the connector with your thumbs while you squeeze to persuade the connector away from its mate. Try to make contact with as much connector, not wire, as possible.

There are many videos on YouTube which are instructive for newbies. Especially helpful even for an experienced guy like me was one video that showed how to restore a stuck motor to working condition with a pair of pliers. Especially learn how to reset the gyros with the transmitter and how to zero-out the transmitter itself. Read the instructions carefully and you'll see that you can adjust the sensitivity of the transmitter relative to control input. Learn and understand how to use the trim buttons. There is a lot of info in that little manual. It's not the greatest manual I've seen, but it is a good effort at one and most of the hazy parts are cleared up on YouTube.

I've found that when the lights flash during flight to signal a low battery (time to land!) that the voltage is about 3.7 volts. This is a pretty safe voltage for storing a LiPo so if you are not going to fly again soon don't bother to charge it. Letting a fully charged LiPo sit for more than a week can be hard on it. Take good care of the battery by never flying it to the point where it is dead. In fact, as soon as you get the flashing warning - land! If you are flying outside where you can't see the warning well in daylight, I'd recommend setting a kitchen timer set to 5-1/2 minutes and timing your flights. Better safe than sorry. Once you run a LiPo down too far it's gone or soon will be.

If you have spare batteries all charged up during a flying session, avoid the temptation of replacing an exhausted battery with a fresh one and getting right back up into the air. My opinion is you should let the motors cool down for a few minutes first. They will be very hot after you complete a full flight so give them a chance to cool a bit before you take to the skies again.

They sell higher capacity batteries here on Amazon. I believe they are 500 mAh. I would not recommend them. Any longer flight time potential will be offset by the extra battery weight. Also the motors will have to work harder at higher RPM to keep the quad airborne. I think the stock capacity battery size is well-suited to this quad.

The instructions encourage you to stuff the battery leads up into the copter body so they don't hang out. I just let them hang out. Stuffing them up in there just stresses all the connections and solder joints and the wires don't stay up in there very will anyway. Just my opinion on that one, folks.

The motors are amazing on these little quads. They are good for about 70 hours of actual flying time. That's really pretty good. Still, if you are going to use the quad a lot and put about 100 flights on it, you will eventually have a motor go bad. It is a good idea to have a spaare motor kit. The motors on the 107C are 8.5mm wide. The motors from the 107L will NOT fit. So get the correct ones.

If you have to replace a motor, you'll have to be able to solder or know somebody who can do it for you. It's a simple soldering task for an experienced RC hobbyist so members of that ilk will have no problem. If you are just leaping into RC with this quad and don't have those skills because you haven't had to suffer the school of hard knocks like we old-timers did, you just have to learn soldering or lean on somebody who can do it for you. Some solder and a basic pencil soldering iron can be obtained for less that 20 bucks if you want to learn a new, useful skill.

As for the HD camera, it is quite sufficient. This little camera will never be super stable outdoors in wind but the video is still quite good. In windy conditions, you MUST press down the right stick to get into expert mode. If you don't you will not have sufficient control movement to fight the wind. You will watch helplessly as your copter drifts away from you if you can't bring it down immediately. Incidentally, while in expert mode if you are afraid of flipping the copter because of the unlimited control movement it provides, just click the left stick down to enter "no-flip" mode.

Also regarding the camera, you must follow the correct procedure to obtain video. Turn on your transmitter with the throttle completely off. Insert the SD card. Connect the battery. Wait for the red light to turn off in the SD card slot. All you should see is a tiny blue light (NO red light). Now you can press the little switch on the side to start recording. You'll see the tiny red light flashing. When you finish your video flight, you must press the little switch again to stop the video. Wait for the red light to go out (indicating the video file has been saved. Now you may unplug the battery. If desired you may also unplug the SD card now.

If you don't use the switch to stop the video, or if you unplug the battery while the red light is flashing, you will save no video.

Always plug/unplug the SD card with the battery disconnected! Also, the SD card socket is not like those on many mobile phones with which you may be familiar. There is no "spring action". You just slide the card in until it bottoms in the slot. If you keep pushing it when you feel resistance thinking you are going to push against the locking spring, don't do it. Push too hard and you could harm the card socket. So go easy on it!

It is amazing that we can now buy a gyro-stabilized copter and get it hovering with so little "learning". It was not unusual for people to spend weeks just learning the touch to get a single rotor copter off the ground in one piece and into a hover. Now it is so much cheaper and simpler. I won't say easy, because as I have said if you are absolute noob you have to learn the controls and develop your skills. Still, you should be able to get it off the ground and hover without too much agony.

If you are interested in flying RC, I don't think you can go wrong with giving this quad a try. I feel it is a bargain price and rewarding and fun to learn to fly.

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Math - Preschool Math Workbook to Learn Counting & Colors with Interactive Activities, Classroom Essentials, Ages 3+ We are really loving these Hot Dots learning activity books. My preschooler loves to count, so this math book is great for getting some counting practice in. I never worked on pattern recognition, and this book includes that, so I’m so glad we’re getting some exposure with that (i.e. circle, circle, square, circle, circle —insert what comes next). It also covers big and small, shapes, the most and the least themes, heavy and light, as well as matching. There’s a lot to learn in this workbook, and it’s a lot of fun.

Two areas of improvement: The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Math - Preschool Math Workbook to Learn Counting & Colors with Interactive Activities, Classroom Essentials, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

text_fidelity_a:
Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays I bought two packs of these bubble guns for a birthday party. You receive 2 pink guns and 3 blue guns in each pack. They are clear and have noise and lights.

Of the 10 bubble guns I received, 2 were defective. There is a lever that moves up and down to produce the bubbles. The lever is supposed to move when the trigger is pressed. For one of the defective bubble guns the lever was so tight that it rarely moved hence no bubbles. For the second defective bubble gun the rubber tubing was run the wrong way down the front of the gun so the rubber tube is very short. It produces bubbles but only when immersed in liquid in the bottle. It also spills a large amount of bubble liquid because of the defective tubing. After a short while it stops working because the bubble solution is too low in the bottle. My hand was also covered in solution at this point.

For the remainder of the bubble guns the rubber tubing is too long and they will not produce bubbles. The tubing is pressed against the side of the bubble container and is unable to siphon up the bubble liquid. The solution is to either push the tubing back up into the gun to make it about 1/4 inch shorter or to snip the end of the tubing by about 1/8 inch. The remaining 8 guns worked after I pushed the tubing higher.

I recommend you test the guns before handing them to children. I bought them for a birthday party so I tested them ahead of time to prevent disappointment.

These are different than battery operated bubble guns. For one thing, the lever has to be pressed about three times each time to produce bubbles in most of the bubble guns. For a few of the bubble guns a slow steady press produced a steady stream of bubbles but most of the triggers are too loose to allow a slow press. So the quality is inconsistent.

I paid $15.99 per box so from a value perspective I wasted about $6.36 because of the defective guns. I'll probably return one box.

UPDATE: Amazon shipped two replacement boxes but 5 of the 10 replacement guns were defective. I could not get them to work no matter how hard or long I tried. I shipped the defective bubble guns back. I will repeat my advice. Test each gun if you are using them for a party or event. Buy early enough so you have time to have replacements shipped to you. The ones that did work, worked beautifully. The kids enjoyed them.
text_fidelity_b: Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:f267642283bcf2ef6b127013dc46be9b]] On the advertising, this says that it shoots 20 feet. I was really skeptical, and I was expecting it to only shoot 20 feet in the air. Now, I don't have a 20 foot ladder, so I can't tell for sure, but I'm pretty sure that this will shoot vertically 20 feet, and horizontally maybe even a little more.

The truck is big and bulky, which I really liked. And there are no small, removable parts, so it's probably good for kids of any age. It does shoot a pretty powerful stream of water, so the only danger is squirting friends, family, and pets in the eye.

Now, about the water, the truck doesn't hold very much water. It says that it will shoot 50 shots of water, and it does do that. This is a lot like one of those water conserving showers. It really doesn't use very much water, but you can't really tell that until you fill it up. So, it's not the best thing for a water fight. But it is a great gift for youngsters so they don't get their siblings too wet. And I did really like the bright, vivid colors.

The wheels rotate, but they can't turn. If you need to turn this, you'll need to pick it up and move it around. Really, the only movable part on this is the fire hose.

Pros:
+Big and bulky
+Fun for all ages
+Shoots water a long way
+You can position the fire hose a little

Cons:
-A little hard to aim
-Wheels can't turn right or left, only rotate straight ahead
-Doesn't hold a ton of water
-You can't build up pressure to do a power squirt
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig
